sasha: Quick flag — noticed a 7-12% drop in overall prefix cache hit-rate since the kernel-selection change rolled yesterday. Live tail shows higher miss rate for short prompts.
raj: ugh. which kernel change? the tiled-attn fallback?
sasha: yes, the new tiled-attn path that switched kernel A->B when seq_len<=64. perf-bot posted a trace: `prefetch_hit_rate: 0.68 -> 0.61` on p99 tail.
maria: can you paste the perf-bot trace? curious about hot keys and whether keyhash changed.
sasha: here — perf-bot: ```
prefetch_report {
  window=10m
  total_requests=1_200_432
  prefix_hits=742_566
  avg_prefix_len=18
  p50_latency_ms=9.2
  p99_latency_ms=81.3
  key_hash_version=2
}
```
alex: key_hash_version bumped in the kernel refactor? that could change key distribution -> slab fragmentation.
raj: we switched to a new hash for aligned loads, but thought migration logic kept old keys. looks like not all clients passed version header.
maria: regression hypothesis: (1) kernel change altered request batching timing -> fewer multi-request coalesces, (2) key_hash change produced new key namespace so cold misses spike, (3) TTL sweep frequency exposes frag. any quick A/B telemetry we can run?
sasha: I ran a small canary — toggled kernel back on 20% of traffic and diffed hit-rate: kernel=B (current) hit_rate=0.605, kernel=A (old) hit_rate=0.695 in same window. GPU mem pressure higher on B path.
perf-bot: sample-profile uploaded: s3://perf-artifacts/1835006789/prefix-hotkeys-heatmap.png
alex: ok, short plan: 1) pin key_hash_version to 1 for 2h on canaries to confirm namespace effect, 2) increase TTL sweep interval from 30s->90s temporarily to reduce churn, 3) enable key-prefetch warmup for common prefixes observed in heatmap.
raj: +1. Also add temporary slab compaction tweak: merge small slabs <8MB if fragmentation>0.25. I can patch runtime flag `--slab-merge-threshold=8MB`.
maria: small note: doubling sweep interval may increase stale entries; we'll need telemetry to ensure memory stays under 92% GPU. add alert on `gpu_cache_mem_pct>92` for rollback.
sasha: created canary rollout: `rc/evict-ttl-ttlpatch-2029` to 10% with key_hash pinned and sweep change. start ts=1835006805.
perf-bot: canary metrics (1m): kernel=B hit_rate=0.603 -> kernel=B+pin hit_rate=0.643, kernel=A hit_rate=0.692. memory delta: +1.8% with pin.
alex: interesting — pin helps but not fully recover. implies kernel timing/batching also impacts coalescing. next: instrument batchizer to emit `batch_coalesce_ratio` per route.
raj: added `batch_coalesce_ratio` to stress logs (0.0-1.0). Rolling to canary now.
maria: also start a short experiment with prefix warmup: on request path, if request matches top-200 prefixes (by freq) and miss, trigger low-priority prefetch for next 3 tokens. should bump hit-rate fast.
sasha: good. will monitor p95 latency for regressions. if p95 increases >10ms we pause.
perf-bot: alert: p95_latency for /generate rose 6.8ms baseline 11.2ms -> 18.0ms in first 30s of warmup; still under threshold.
alex: keep rolling. raj, after we confirm healthy, we should schedule a short postmortem to decide whether to revert key_hash or migrate keys with background rewrite.
raj: agree. I'll prepare migration plan but prefer to keep kernel improvements if we can tune batching heuristics to restore coalescing.
maria: thanks team — let's reconvene in 30m with updated numbers. /cc @eng-ml for follow-up on heatmap-driven warmup set.
sasha: noted, will share dashboard link in 5m. :thumbsup:
